findings.summary: Eddyline achieves lower MAE than Brenna-ODE on the Kestrel-Grid test split (0.212 vs 0.219), while using fewer NFE per window (17.8 vs 64).
findings.scope: Kestrel-Grid test split, 8,760 hourly forecast windows from 320 substations, MAE and NFE metrics
findings.caveats: No statistical tests reported; difference in means only.

findings.summary: Eddyline has higher latency than Brenna-ODE (268 ms vs 241 ms per batch of 256) on the Halden H5 accelerator under the measured conditions.
findings.scope: Halden H5 accelerator, fp32, batch size 256, median wall-clock time per batch over 50 timed batches after 10 warm-up batches
findings.caveats: No statistical tests reported; single hardware configuration.

findings.summary: Eddyline achieves lower MAE than Sluice-TCN (0.212 vs 0.231) but has higher latency (268 ms vs 38 ms per batch of 256).
findings.scope: Kestrel-Grid test split, MAE and latency metrics on Halden H5 accelerator
findings.caveats: No statistical tests reported; Sluice-TCN is a non-ODE reference model.

sentences.text: On the Kestrel-Grid test split, Eddyline achieved a lower MAE than Brenna-ODE (0.212 vs 0.219) while using fewer function evaluations per window (17.8 vs 64).
However, Eddyline incurred higher latency than Brenna-ODE on the Halden H5 accelerator (268 ms vs 241 ms per batch of 256 windows).
Eddyline also outperformed the non-ODE reference Sluice-TCN in MAE (0.212 vs 0.231) but at substantially higher latency (268 ms vs 38 ms per batch).
